amendments.rule: **Where a privative `מִן` + infinitive construct is recast as a negative result clause, the preposition takes the frame's function words and the infinitive takes its supplied subject.** The ASV writes *that it cannot save*, *so that he will not hear*, *that I should give*. The complementizer and the negation are what the `מִן` contributes and stay with it, including a *cannot* that fuses that negation with the modal and so cannot be divided; the supplied subject pronoun, and any modal the ASV writes as a separate word, belong to the infinitive, exactly as rule 17 keeps a subject pronoun with its verb and as the corpus does after any preposition — `לָמוּת` → *that he should die*, `מִתִּתִּי` → *that* on the preposition beside *should give* on the infinitive. The two units may interleave — *that*(`מִן`) *it*(inf.) *cannot*(`מִן`) *save*(inf.) — which rule 25 allows; do not hand the preposition the subject pronoun merely to keep its unit contiguous. Where the ASV supplies no negation at all the `מִן` keeps only the complementizer. **And the negation is the `מִן`'s only where no negative morpheme stands in the clause to carry it.** Where the privative stands on an existential `אַיִן`, that particle is what the ASV's negation word realizes: it takes that word and heads on it under rule 50, while the `מִן` keeps only the complementizer the ASV has written — `מֵאֵין עוֹבֵר` → *so that none shall pass through* gives *so that* to the `מִן` and *none* to the `אַיִן`, a present morpheme taking its English before a supplied reading does, exactly as in rules 46 and 47. What the privative governs need not be an infinitive construct: an `אַיִן` with a participle or a noun after it is read the same way. But where the ASV spends a single English word on the preposition and the particle together — `מֵאֵין` → *without* — the one-English-word condition of rule 30 is met and the two share one unit instead, headed on the negation.
amendments.why: Rule 48 as written says flatly that the complementizer and the negation are both the privative `מִן`'s, and rule 50 says the existential `אַיִן` heads on the negation word. `מֵאֵין עוֹבֵר` at EZK.33.28 → *so that none shall pass through* is the first place in this testament's chapters where the two claims land on the same English word, and the rule as it stood would have given *none* to the preposition and left a written `אַיִן` `unrepresented`. The chapter resolved it by the contract's own recurring principle — a present morpheme takes its English before a supplied reading does, stated already in rules 14, 16, 41, 44, 46 and 47 — so the amendment narrows rule 48 rather than adding a rule that points back at it. Two further gaps are closed in the same breath, both met by this verse: the privative's complement here is a particle plus participle rather than an infinitive construct, and the common `מֵאֵין` → *without* is carved out to rule 30 so that the new sentence cannot be read as splitting a single English word. No corpus row shown for `מִן` or `אַיִן` treats the construction the other way, and rule 50's own count of 28 existential units heads every one on the negation, which is what the amendment preserves.

conventions: In the title `אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה` the ASV's *the Lord* is the noun `אֲדֹנָי` together with the supplied *the* that determines it (rule 15), the `Sp1cs` suffix is `unrepresented` because the ASV writes no possessive for it, and `יְהוִה` takes *Jehovah*; in a construct the rectum's *of* joins the same unit (*of the Lord*). Applied at 33.11, 33.17, 33.20, 33.25, 33.27. BSB represents the suffix, which is a convention difference and not an error.

Where two particles are fused into one English word under rule 30, this chapter heads the unit on the morpheme whose sense that word most directly carries, and on the opening particle where neither morpheme does: `כָּל … לֹא` → *none* (33.13, 33.16) and `וְ … לֹא` → *neither* (33.12) head on the negative, as rule 35 heads *Nor*, while `אִם לֹא` → *surely* (33.27) heads on the oath particle and `כִּי אִם` → *but* (33.11) on `כִּי`. Every one of these units names the competing head in its note.

Every rule 30 fusion in this chapter is filed `aligned`; the chapter records no `noncompositional` unit (33.12 *thereby*, 33.13 and 33.18 *therein*, 33.21 *twelfth*, 33.22 and 33.31 `לִפְנֵי` → *before*, 33.25 `לָכֵן` → *Wherefore*, 33.29 `עַל` → *because of*, 33.30 `מֵאֵת` → *from*, 33.33 `בְּתוֹךְ` → *among*). The corpus files `לִפְנֵי` → *before* both ways (143 aligned, 220 noncompositional), so this is a chapter-uniform choice rather than a correction of either.

For rule 55's count this chapter reads *whereas* and *if* as two subordinating words rather than as the coordinator-plus-subordinator pair that rule exempts: `וְהוּא נִזְהָר` → *whereas if he had taken warning* (33.5) gives *whereas* to the waw and leaves the *if* `added`, and `וְרָאָה` → *if when he seeth* (33.3) gives *if* to the waw and leaves the *when* `added`. The pair reading, which would give both words to the waw and mark nothing `added`, is named in each unit's note and is the likelier place a later reader will disagree.

report: Read all 63 candidate groups and the full verse dump end to end (verses 1-33 all present). No construction in this chapter is analysed two ways: every multi-treatment bucket is the ASV writing a different English word for the same morpheme in a different clause, which the source licenses. patches is empty.

Checks that could have hidden a split and did not: article counting in construct chains is uniform (one written *the* goes to the present article at 33.6, 33.15, 33.27; two written *the*s split construct/article at 33.2, 33.4, 33.5, 33.11, 33.12, 33.30; no article morpheme means a supplied *the* on the construct at 33.1, 33.7, 33.10, 33.12, 33.17, 33.20, 33.22, 33.23, 33.28, 33.30). The infinitive-absolute intensifier takes *surely* as its own unit at 33.8, 33.13, 33.14, 33.15, 33.16. A suffix on an infinitive takes the subject pronoun at 33.8, 33.13, 33.14, 33.29, 33.33, and 33.22's suffixless `עַד־בּוֹא` correctly keeps its supplied *he* on the infinitive. `בְּ`+suffix and `עַל`+suffix fuse to *therein*/*thereby* at 33.12, 33.13, 33.18, 33.19 without exception.

The added units are the one place the candidate table is blind, so I read them against the whole chapter. All eight are coherent: *as for* is `added` at 33.12, 33.17 and 33.30 (each fronted phrase is a bare construct or bare pronoun with no marker and no preposition, rule 16's second and third limits) and is never folded into a neighbouring morpheme anywhere in the chapter; a supplied subordinator goes to a present conjunction wherever one stands (33.2, 33.6, 33.9, 33.13, 33.14, 33.29, 33.33) and is `added` only where the ASV's subordinators outnumber the clause's conjunctions (33.3, 33.5, 33.13, 33.15); the second *but* at 33.31 has no waw in its clause while every other *but* does.

Weakest accepted edge, flagged rather than changed: 33.5's `added` *if* in *whereas if*. If *whereas* is read as the connective the waw takes under rule 14's open list, then *whereas if* is a connective plus a subordinator written together at the recast clause's left edge, which is rule 55's pair clause and would give both words to the waw with nothing `added`. The verse note names that reading; 33.3's *if when* is two subordinators on any reading and is a surplus either way. I left both as accepted since the chapter treats them alike and rule 55's exemption is worded for a coordinator plus a subordinator.

BSB: 29 disagreements, all documented convention differences and none a genuine error. The R x8 group is `לֵאמֹר`'s `לְ` (rule 27); Sp1cs x5 is the suffix of `אֲדֹנָי`; the `אֵת` rows are rule 16's ordinary unrepresented marker; 33.3 and 33.6 `בַּ` is rule 40 (the ASV promotes the object: *blow the trumpet*), with the assimilated article still taking its *the*; 33.2 `הָ` and 33.27's two suffixes are resumptive under rule 22; 33.4 `שָׁמַע` is the finite verb of `וְשָׁמַע הַשֹּׁמֵעַ`, rendered once; 33.10 `כִּי` is genuinely unrendered in the ASV text (its margin reads 'Truly'); Td x4 is rule 41's limit, where a demonstrative or possessive already carries the phrase's one determiner.

33.2's `אֶחָד` (`אִישׁ אֶחָד` -> *a man*) is left `unrepresented` with the indefinite article on the noun under rule 15. Rule 30's generic-head-noun clause would instead fuse `אִישׁ אֶחָד` into one unit; either reading spends the same English, so the ledger is unaffected and I did not disturb it.

One amendment returned, to rule 48. `מֵאֵין עוֹבֵר` at 33.28 is the first place where rule 48's 'the negation stays with the `מִן`' meets a written `אַיִן` that rule 50 says carries the negation word; the chapter split them (*so that* on the preposition, *none* on the particle) and the amendment records that a present negative morpheme takes the word, with rule 30 fusion carved out for `מֵאֵין` -> *without*.

No promotions. The other chapter-wide judgments -- the `אֲדֹנָי` title, the head of a fused particle pair, filing rule-30 fusions as `aligned`, and reading *whereas* as a subordinator for rule 55's count -- are recorded as conventions instead: each is an application decision on a particular word rather than a rule that would generalise, and the corpus already handles the first three both ways or not at all.
